overall: The AG found the Planning Board and Board of Selectmen did not violate the Open Meeting Law by meeting in Purpose 3 executive session on March 14, 2011, because litigation was reasonably anticipated and the discussion stayed on litigation consequences.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the March 14, 2011 joint executive session to discuss 'threatened litigation' over an AT&T matter had no pending or threatened litigation and no proper basis.
allegations.key_passage: Despite this statement, looking at all that transpired prior to that date, it was reasonable for Attorney Cantor to anticipate litigation in response to certain actions the Boards might take, and to advise the Boards of the potential legal consequences of these actions.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session was used to decide or discuss the merits of AT&T's consultant-fee appeal, which must occur in open session.
allegations.key_passage: While the executive session minutes reflect some discussion of the appeal and the Board's options in deciding it, it appears the discussion focused on the litigation consequences and not the merits of AT&T's appeal.
